channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Education Infrastructure Transformed Over Seven Years
item.description: Over the past seven years, Kazakhstan has significantly developed its education infrastructure, increasing student capacity and reducing triple-shift and dilapidated schools. Since 2019, 1,342 new schools have been built, creating 1.1 million student places. The national project 'Future Schools' has added 217 new schools.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Allow Citizens to Appeal to Administrative Courts Before Rights Are Violated
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering allowing citizens and businesses to appeal to administrative courts before their rights are violated, aiming to prevent unlawful actions by state bodies. This proposal is part of a new draft of the Administrative Court Procedure Code, which passed its first reading in the Legislative Chamber. The changes would introduce four types of administrative claims: challenging, prohibiting, obligating, and recognizing.

item.title: Mirmansur Mirxamidov Appointed First Deputy Minister of Internal Affairs of Uzbekistan
item.description: Mirmansur Mirxamidov has been appointed as the First Deputy Minister of Internal Affairs and Head of the Operational-Investigative Department of Uzbekistan. He succeeds Botir Qudratxo‘jayev, who was appointed Minister of Defense on October 12.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Increase Minimum Wage to 110,000 Tenge by 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to raise the minimum wage from 85,000 to 110,000 tenge starting in 2027, potentially affecting 1.8 million people. This increase could also impact the maximum limits for social payments related to childcare, unemployment, and maternity, as well as social contributions and pension deductions. Economists caution that wage growth may not fully restore purchasing power and could add pressure on prices.

item.title: Road and Transport Workers Honored in West Kazakhstan Region
item.description: A ceremony and concert were held in Oral to honor workers in the road and automobile transport sectors. The regional governor highlighted President Tokayev's emphasis on developing transport infrastructure to strengthen transit potential and boost the economy. Significant road construction and repair projects are underway in the region.

item.title: Central Asian Countries Decline to Host Western Military Bases
item.description: Central Asian nations are reportedly refusing to host Western military bases on their territories. This decision comes amid evolving geopolitical dynamics in the region, with countries prioritizing their own security and regional stability over foreign military presence.

item.title: Kazakh MP Warns 16% VAT Rate May Not Meet Revenue Expectations
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kazakhstan has expressed concerns that the current 16% Value Added Tax (VAT) rate may not generate the anticipated revenue. Olzhas Kuspekov stated that the government already acknowledges the situation and believes the state budget has fallen short of planned income. He anticipates that by early 2027, it will be clear that the new VAT rate has not met expectations.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Modernize Infrastructure with 6.5 Trillion Tenge from National Fund
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced a plan to allocate 6.5 trillion tenge from the National Fund by the end of 2029 for infrastructure modernization. The initiative includes social, transport, and engineering projects, with 1.5 trillion tenge earmarked for social projects in 2027.

item.title: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev Delivers Address to the Nation on New Historical Stage
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has published his traditional address to the people of Kazakhstan, titled 'Urgent Tasks of Kazakhstan in a New Historical Era.' The address follows recent national celebrations, including Republic Day and the adoption of the Constitution, marking significant political and institutional reforms.

item.title: Iran Claims Samarkand Heritage Posts Targeted U.S. Amid Diplomatic Dispute with Uzbekistan
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry stated that its embassies' social media posts about Samarkand's Persian heritage were directed at the United States, following a diplomatic protest from Uzbekistan demanding their removal. Uzbekistan objected to posts describing the city's architecture as part of Persian civilization. Iran emphasized its importance for relations with Uzbekistan.

item.title: Bishkek to Fine Bus Drivers for Traffic Violations
item.description: Bishkek Mayor Aibek Dzhunushaliev has ordered stricter controls on public transport drivers. Fines will be issued for traffic violations, to be paid by the drivers themselves. This measure comes amid an increase in bus-related accidents. New buses are being procured, and cashless payment is being implemented to reduce driver distraction.

item.title: Uzbekistan Health Ministry Discloses Compensation for 'Dok-1 Max' and 'Ambronol' Victims
item.description: Uzbekistan's Health Ministry announced compensation payments for families affected by 'Dok-1 Max' and 'Ambronol' medications. Initially, 82 billion soums were to be collected from convicts. However, only 20% was recovered. President Mirziyoyev ordered expedited payments, allocating the remaining 65.2 billion soums from the state budget.

item.title: EAEU Companies to Gain Broader Access to Each Other's Public Procurement
item.description: Companies from Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) member states will be able to participate more broadly in public procurement processes within the union. This initiative aims to enhance economic integration and provide greater opportunities for businesses operating within the EAEU framework.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sees Tenge Depreciation Against US Dollar
item.description: The US dollar's exchange rate in Kazakhstan increased by 1.1 tenge, reaching 457.09 tenge on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange (KASE). The National Bank's official rate stands at 455.63 tenge. Exchange offices in Astana and Almaty reported varying rates for the dollar, euro, and ruble.

item.title: Tajikistan Introduces New Migration Law with Age Restrictions
item.description: Tajikistan's new migration law introduces significant changes, including a ban on labor migration for individuals under 18. The article promises a detailed and clear explanation of these new regulations and their implications for migrant workers.

item.title: Uzbekistan Among World Leaders in Poverty Reduction, Says Official
item.description: Uzbekistan is among the world's leading countries in poverty reduction, according to Deputy Minister of Employment Marat Juraev. He stated that the World Bank ranks the country among the top five globally for its pace of poverty reduction.

item.title: Head of Samruk-Energo Dismissed Over Unsatisfactory Project Implementation
item.description: The head of Samruk-Energo, Kairat Maksutov, has been dismissed from his position. The decision by Samruk-Kazyna's board cited unsatisfactory progress on strategic investment projects and insufficient oversight of new power generation capacity construction. Maksutov had led the company since June 2023.

item.title: Legal Inspector of Water Supply Company Arrested for Bribery in Khorezm
item.description: A legal inspector for the "Khorezm suv ta'minoti" joint-stock company was arrested while receiving a bribe of 6 million soms. The inspector allegedly promised to connect a citizen's trade outlet to the drinking water network for a fee.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Small business employees earn significantly less than national average
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan, the average monthly salary for employees of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in 2025 was 34,643 som, significantly lower than the national average of 42,493 som. This represents an 18.5% difference. Despite this gap, salaries in SMEs have grown 2.7 times since 2021. SMEs contribute 50.9% to the country's GDP.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission to engage youth in civic life
item.description: The Central Election Commission of Kyrgyzstan plans to collaborate with the Bishkek mayor's office to enhance civic activity and legal literacy among schoolchildren and youth. A meeting discussed joint initiatives to foster legal culture, civic responsibility, and youth involvement in public life. A memorandum of cooperation is expected.

item.title: East Kazakhstan Airports Construction Continues to Fulfill State of the Nation Address Goals
item.description: The construction of Zaisan and Katonkaragay airports in East Kazakhstan is progressing, aiming to enhance regional connectivity and boost tourism. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev emphasized the importance of developing transport infrastructure, including these airports, to transform Kazakhstan into a leading Eurasian transport and logistics hub.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's SMEs Contribute Over Half of the Country's GDP
item.description: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Kyrgyzstan accounted for 50.9% of the country's GDP in 2025, according to the National Statistical Committee. The total value added by SMEs reached over 1 trillion soms, a significant increase from previous years. Despite this, average salaries in SMEs remain below the national average.

item.title: Kazakh MP Calls for Verification of State Information System Data Accuracy
item.description: A member of the Kurultai, Askhat Aimagambetov, has proposed verifying the accuracy of data within state information systems, citing concerns about decisions being made based on potentially unreliable information. He stated that implementing new social assistance approaches falls under the government's purview and can be managed through by-laws.

item.title: Kazakhstan Detains Woman for Posting Separatist Video, Investigation Launched
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) has detained a resident of the Pavlodar region for publishing a video with separatist content. An investigation has been initiated. The woman has a prior conviction for drug trafficking.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Economic Climate Resilience and Green Development Prospects Discussed in Tashkent
item.description: An international seminar on water and climate risks' impact on Uzbekistan's economy and green development opportunities was held in Tashkent on October 27, 2026. Organized by the Institute of Macroeconomic and Regional Studies and Russia's HSE University, it gathered government bodies, research centers, and financial institutions from both countries.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Proposes Higher Taxes for the Wealthy
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has proposed discussing a higher tax rate for individuals with substantial wealth. He emphasized that this aims for a fair contribution to the country's development. The government and Parliament will study the proposal, with details on the new rate yet to be specified.

item.title: US Cryptocurrency Exchange Kraken Receives Preliminary Approval in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kraken, a US-based cryptocurrency exchange, has secured preliminary approval to operate within the Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC). The company aims to launch a trading platform and hold digital assets for customers, pending the acquisition of its final license. This move aligns with Kazakhstan's increasing oversight of crypto trading platforms.

item.title: Jizzakh Region Prepares Gas Networks for Autumn-Winter Season
item.description: The Jizzakh region is implementing measures to ensure stable gas supply for the 2026-2027 autumn-winter period. Over 85 kilometers of gas pipelines have been reconstructed, exceeding the planned 68.9 kilometers. Additionally, 3,224 gas distribution points have been inspected, and 171.4 kilometers of pipelines tested. Gas systems in over 21,000 homes were modernized.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Samruk-Energo Head Dismissed After President's Criticism
item.description: The head of Kazakhstan's Samruk-Energo, Kairat Maksutov, has been dismissed following criticism from President Tokayev. The reasons for the dismissal were not immediately specified, but it follows a period of public scrutiny of the energy sector.

item.title: Tajikistan Proposes Tourism and Processing Development to Qatari Investors
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Economic Development and Trade met with Qatari business leaders to discuss expanding bilateral cooperation in tourism, industry, and product processing. Discussions included joint ventures in special economic zones and processing agricultural products for export to Qatar.

item.title: Nearly 540 Deaths in Kyrgyzstan Attributed to Traffic Accidents in Eight Months
item.description: In the first eight months of the year, approximately 540 individuals in Kyrgyzstan died due to traffic accidents. The National Statistical Committee reported that out of 21,300 total deaths, cardiovascular diseases were the leading cause, followed by neoplasms and respiratory illnesses.

item.title: Nine 'Terrorists' Killed in Pakistan's Balochistan Province, Army Claims
item.description: The Pakistani army announced that nine 'terrorists' were killed in two operations in the southern province of Balochistan, bordering Afghanistan. The army identified the deceased as members of the 'India-backed Balochistan Liberation Front.' The operations, conducted in Kachhi and Udhir districts, resulted in the seizure of weapons and ammunition. Pakistan alleges that militants use Afghan territory for attacks.

item.title: Uzbekistan Secures $300 Million in Loans for Power Grid Upgrades
item.description: Uzbekistan has secured $300 million in loans from the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank to modernize 60 electrical substations. The upgrades aim to reduce power outages and losses, facilitating the integration of new renewable energy sources. The government will contribute an additional $71 million to the $371 million total program cost. These improvements are crucial for meeting growing electricity demand and Uzbekistan's renewable energy targets.

item.title: Kazakh MP Explains Funding for Budget Employee Salary Increases
item.description: Kazakh Member of Parliament Askhat Aimagambetov clarified that salary increases for budget employees, including approximately 77,000 doctors, will be funded through additional budget allocations and government reserves. The proposed changes to the three-year budget project aim to raise minimum wages and provide a roughly 40% increase for medical professionals starting January 1st.

item.title: Afghanistan's Taliban government reports 44 large-scale mining contracts are active
item.description: The Taliban's mines minister announced that 44 large-scale mining contracts are active in Afghanistan, with a total of 350 mining contracts operational. Approximately 180,000 people are employed in the sector. The government is promoting mining to boost investment and revenue amid economic challenges.

item.title: Former presidential aide Zarif Alizoda appointed head of Tajikistan's election commission
item.description: Zarif Alizoda, a former presidential aide, has been appointed as the new head of Tajikistan's Central Commission for Elections and Referendums. His candidacy was approved by the lower house of parliament. This appointment comes less than a year before the next presidential elections, scheduled for 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan MP Proposes Defining Middle Class by Savings of Over 5 Million Tenge
item.description: Kazakh Member of Parliament Aidos Sarym suggested defining the middle class in Kazakhstan based on savings, proposing individuals with over 5 million tenge in savings be considered separately. He argued that a broad definition of the middle class could lead to instability, emphasizing the need for institutional and economic stability. Sarym also noted the importance of savings for family support in case of unforeseen events.

item.title: Kazakh Tenge Depreciates Against US Dollar by 1.1 Tenge in One Day
item.description: The US dollar strengthened against the Kazakh tenge, closing at 457.09 tenge on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange (KASE) on October 28. This marks an increase of 1.1 tenge in a single day. Average exchange rates at currency exchange offices in Kazakhstan showed the dollar buying at 455-455.7 tenge and selling at 456-457 tenge.

item.title: Authorities Explain Rogun HPS Incident; Reports of Injured Workers Emerge
item.description: Authorities have explained an incident at the Rogun Hydropower Plant (HPS), attributing it to the collapse of a technical water collection basin. However, Radio Ozodi reports, citing its sources, that over five plant workers were injured in the event.

item.title: Afghan Orchard Owners Face Plummeting Grape Prices Amidst Taliban Taxes and Storage Shortages
item.description: Orchard owners in Afghanistan's Koh Daman region are struggling with falling grape prices, a lack of cold storage, and limited market access. Many are forced to sell produce below production cost, unable to recover expenses. Experts warn that inadequate storage and market access restrict horticultural exports and reduce farmer income.
